descs.t: Abdul El-Sayed has won the US Senate race in Michigan, defeating Republican Mike Rogers and becoming the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. His win came on a night when Democrats took control of both the House and the Senate. We walk through the result, his victory speech and what the new Senate looks like.

Abdul El-Sayed is Michigan's senator-elect and the first Muslim elected to the US Senate, and his victory speech went straight at JD Vance and Donald Trump. Vance now says the reason Republicans lost is the war. We look at what El-Sayed said, why Republicans lost both chambers, and who is claiming the result.

Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan and told JD Vance he is constitutionally obligated to swear him in, then told Trump to just call him senator. Democrats took the House and the Senate, Texas elected a Democratic senator, and Vance blamed the war. We break down the night, the speech and who is celebrating it.

intro.plain: Abdul El-Sayed has won the Senate race in Michigan, beating Republican Mike Rogers, and he becomes the first Muslim elected to the US Senate. That came on the same night Democrats took control of both the House and the Senate. So the Senate that Trump works with in January looks very different. Tell me in the chat: did you expect Democrats to take both chambers?

Chat, who really lost this election, Trump or the war?

descs.t: Republicans are blaming Senate Majority Leader John Thune for their 2026 midterm losses. Byron Donalds and Nancy Mace say failing to pass the SAVE America Act cost the party, while posts say Democrats took 54 Senate seats and at least 228 in the House. We walk through the case against Thune and what Republicans can still do before January 3rd.

John Thune is now the focus of Republican anger after the midterms. Ohio, North Carolina and Nevada passed voter ID amendments even as Republicans lost there, and critics say the SAVE America Act and hundreds of House bills stalled in the Senate. We look at whether the blame fits and what 60 days of Republican control can still pass.

Republicans held the House, the Senate and the White House and still lost the 2026 midterms, and their own base is calling for John Thune to resign. Critics say he stalled the SAVE America Act and left House bills waiting. We go through what went wrong and what the fight inside the party means for the next two years.

intro.plain: Republicans lost big in the midterms, and the anger is already pointed at one man: Senate Majority Leader John Thune. Byron Donalds and Nancy Mace say he cost the party by never passing the SAVE America Act. Posts say Democrats took 54 Senate seats and at least 228 in the House. Is Thune really to blame, or is that too easy? Tell me in the chat.
intro.mid: Here is the strangest part of this election: Ohio voted to require photo ID, and Democrats still swept Ohio. Meanwhile Republicans are blaming John Thune for not passing the SAVE America Act. Republicans still control Congress until January 3rd, about 60 days. So what should they do with that time? Drop your answer in the chat.
intro.bold: Republicans had the House, the Senate and the White House, and they just got dragged through this election. Now their own base is turning on John Thune, calling for him to resign over the SAVE America Act and the House bills critics say he sat on. Was it Thune, or something bigger? Tell me in the chat right now.
